title: Knowledge check: Text and HTML Rendering Directives

questions.prompt: Which approach best matches “Text and HTML Rendering Directives”?
options: Use declarative template bindings and keep expressions small; choose directives according to the intended DOM behavior.
Manually rewrite the DOM for every state change.
Put multi-step business logic directly in template expressions.
Use raw HTML rendering for every value.
questions.answer_key: Use declarative template bindings and keep expressions small; choose directives according to the intended DOM behavior.
questions.explanation: This answer addresses Text and HTML Rendering Directives directly. Verify the behavior in a small Vue 3 example and check the runtime requirements in the linked official reference.

questions.prompt: For “v-text”, which practice is most reliable?
options: v-html is the safe default for user-generated HTML.
v-show always removes the element from the DOM.
Custom directives are the best tool for all component reuse.
Use v-if to create/remove conditional content and v-show when toggling CSS visibility is more appropriate.
questions.answer_key: Use v-if to create/remove conditional content and v-show when toggling CSS visibility is more appropriate.
questions.explanation: This practice supports the syllabus subtopic “v-text”. Check the expected result and a relevant boundary or failure case.

questions.prompt: A learner example for “Text and HTML Rendering Directives” behaves unexpectedly. What should be checked first?
options: Disable error handling and assume the framework is at fault.
Trust a client-supplied success flag without checking behavior.
Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
Change unrelated files until the page looks correct.
questions.answer_key: Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
questions.explanation: Start with a small reproducible case. Inspect the element, reactive source, Console, and expected result before changing unrelated code.
